_notes: COPY THIS FILE, RENAME IT NNN-something.json, FILL IN THE XI. That is the
whole authoring job. Everything else — the scrambles, the pitch layout, the
position labels, the enumerations — is DERIVED by tools/build_scrambled.js.
Nothing here is typed twice. In particular the formation is not a caption:
it is parsed, and the bands, the slot count and the default position labels
come out of it. The draft carried `formation: "4-4-2"` beside a hand-written
band list, which is one fact in two places and would eventually have shipped
a board captioned 4-4-2 and laid out 4-3-3.
ORDER MATTERS. Goalkeeper first, then each line from the back forward, and
each line LEFT TO RIGHT as the viewer sees it. That order is what places
the tiles, so a full-back in the wrong slot is a wrong board.
NAMES ARE AUTHORED IN PLAIN A-Z. No diacritics — write ODEGAARD, not the
accented form. The build refuses anything else, because the scramble is
built from these letters and the player is shown these letters, and a name
pasted off a squad list with a combining mark still in it makes those two
different things.
SHARED SURNAMES MUST CARRY A FORENAME. Two slots whose letters agree are
indistinguishable on the pitch — the player cannot know which CHARLTON goes
where, and neither can the marker. The build refuses it. Author them as
JACK CHARLTON and BOBBY CHARLTON, and do NOT give either the bare surname
as an alias.
hintField is "club" or "nationality" — whichever VARIES across the eleven.
A club XI sells nationality; a national XI or a Team of the Year sells club.
The build refuses a board whose chosen field reads the same for all eleven,
because that hint sells the player something already on their screen.
seed makes the scramble reproducible: same file in, same board out. Use
something meaningful — a date as YYYYMMDD is the convention.
source is not optional. Every board is a claim about who played; it carries
the URL that backs it, and the build refuses a board without one.
title: Short title shown above the pitch
pool: The sentence that tells the player what the eleven IS. Say it plainly — a player who does not know the frame is not solving a puzzle, they are guessing at the whole of football.
